subject: Clarify: residency assurances, transient egress for analytics & latency impacts
thread_content:
From: Alicia White <alicia.white@healthtech.co>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthtech.co, security@healthtech.co
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:23:00 -0400
Subject: Residency commitment and transient egress for analytics — follow-up

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we surface Redwood to our legal and security committees, two items came up that we need clarified in writing: 1) whether our customer data can be constrained to EU-only processing and storage (region pinning) for production workloads, and 2) whether Redwood will perform any transient cross-region processing (e.g., analytics aggregation, edge caching) that would cause data to leave the EU, even temporarily.

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm a binding operational standard for EU-region pinning (what you call "anchoring") and any known transient exceptions?
- For analytics/telemetry (sampling/rollups), do you ever export aggregated metrics outside the EU region? If so, under what conditions and safeguards (encryption, key control)?
- If failover to another region is required for reliability, what is the maximum expected window before data is restored to EU processing?

If helpful, our security team is particularly interested in KMS ownership during any transient hop and a short diagram showing where traffic may traverse.

Appreciate a short written statement we can share with our DPO.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia White
Sr. Security Program Manager — HealthTech Solutions

---

On Mon, Jul 12, 2027 at 12:10 PM Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Alicia White <alicia.white@healthtech.co>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 12:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Residency commitment and transient egress for analytics — follow-up

Hi Alicia,

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: yes, we support EU-region pinning for production workloads; transient cross-region hops can occur under a small set of operational contingencies (brief edge cache population, ephemeral analytics aggregation for platform health), and those are subject to encryption-in-transit and at-rest, with customer-managed KMS options for Private deployments.

I attached a diagram (Data Residency Diagram v2.pdf) and a short SOC2 excerpt to help your DPO. Below I captured a concise set of commitments and the operational caveats so you can copy into your questionnaire.

Redwood EU-region pinning (production) — statement of assurance:
- Production inference and persistent storage for pinned accounts will be anchored to EU datacenters as configured by the customer policy.
- Transient caching: we may populate short-lived edge caches outside the EU to reduce latency for geographically distributed end-users, but cached payloads are TTL-bound (max 2 hours) and encrypted. Cached copies are not retained beyond the TTL for pinned accounts.
- Analytics/telemetry: aggregate platform telemetry and internal metrics that could include hashed identifiers may be processed outside the EU for platform-level analytics; raw customer request/response payloads are not exported. For customers requiring no cross-region telemetry, we offer an opt-out and can route telemetry aggregation to EU-only analytics endpoints for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Failover: conditional failover to a non-EU region is possible if EU capacity is exhausted or in disaster scenarios; the failover window is configurable but our standard SRE playbook targets restoration and reanchoring within 48 hours. Shorter SLOs (24h) can be contracted under Dedicated commitments.
- KMS/key control: for Hosted customers, Redwood manages keys by default but supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private — this ensures control over key material during any transient processing.

Action items if you want a written DPA addendum: 1) we can add clause language around TTL for edge caches, 2) include an explicit telemetry opt-out path, 3) specify max failover window in the SLO appendix.

Looping in Marissa (ops) and Kimberly (legal) to confirm operational runbook timings and suggested clause text.

Thanks,
Sofia
Senior Privacy & Policy — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Residency commitment and transient egress for analytics — follow-up

Hi Alicia — quick ops addendum from our side:

Operational guardrails (more detail):
- Edge cache TTL: 2 hours max for pinned accounts; caches are encrypted with per-service keys and purged on TTL expiry. We log cache population events and can surface those logs in EU-only telemetry for compliance reviews.
- Analytics rollups: we only transfer highly aggregated, non-reversible metrics for platform health unless the customer opts in. Examples: token-rate histograms, error rates (no raw content). For Enterprise/Dedicated we can route aggregation to EU-only endpoints and retain aggregates for 30 days by default.
- Failover protocol: if EU capacity drops below configured thresholds, traffic will failover to the next compatible region. The automated failover window for Hosted customers is immediate (to maintain availability) but reanchoring is automated and targeted to complete within 24-48 hours depending on workload size; we will provide a reanchoring runbook during onboarding.

Attachments: SOC2-Summary-2027.pdf (high level), runbook excerpt to follow in separate email.

If you want, we can run a 30-minute call with our SREs to walk the reanchoring steps and show the logs you would see during the window.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Residency commitment and transient egress for analytics — follow-up

Hi Alicia,

From a contracting perspective, we can offer the following DPA addendum language options — please let us know which fits your risk profile:

Option A (standard): Redwood will implement region pinning for customer production workloads. Transient edge caching and platform aggregation are permitted as described; Redwood will adopt commercially reasonable measures (encryption, access controls). Failover events will be communicated within 24 hours; reanchoring targeted within 48 hours.

Option B (enhanced): Adds: telemetry opt-out by default for all EU-pinned customers; edge cache TTL contractually limited to 2 hours; failed reanchoring (beyond 48h) triggers a remediation credit. Requires Dedicated or Private deployment.

Option C (strict): No cross-region processing of any customer data. This requires Private deployment and customer-managed KMS with attestation and annual audits.

We can draft the addendum corresponding to your preferred option and share a redline.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia — pulling this together so you have a clean bundle for your DPO and procurement. Attached: Data Residency Diagram v2.pdf and SOC2-Summary-2027.pdf.

Summary (copyable):
- Redwood supports EU-region pinning for production workloads. Persistent storage and inference are anchored to EU regions by default for pinned accounts.
- Transient edge caching: occasional short-lived caching outside the EU for latency reduction; TTL = 2 hours, encrypted, and purged at TTL expiry. We can include a contractual TTL cap.
- Analytics/telemetry: platform-level aggregates (non-reversible) may be processed outside EU unless you elect the EU-only telemetry option. Raw request/response data is not exported.
- Failover: automated failover may route traffic to alternate regions to preserve availability; reanchoring targeted within 24-48 hours. Dedicated customers may contract shorter windows and SLO credits.
- KMS: Hosted = Redwood-managed keys by default; Dedicated/Private = customer-managed keys available (BYOK).

Next steps:
1) Which DPA addendum option (A/B/C) do you prefer? We will prepare a redline.
2) If you choose B or C we will schedule an SRE runbook walkthrough and provide sample logs from our repro environment.
3) If helpful, we can provide an evidence package (cache population logs, reanchoring runbook excerpt, SOC2 excerpt) via the Drive link below.
